title: Livepanel metric fanout stall causes intermittent zeroed widgets during failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a cross-region capacity failover last week, multiple customers reported live console widgets showing persistent zeros (0) or stale values for 1-5 minute windows despite upstream telemetry being present. Issue surfaced on Hosted and Dedicated tenants during elevated SLO throttling and burst routing changes.

Impact:
- Several enterprise customers escalated due to SLO/SLA breaches in dashboards used to drive on-call actions (alerts fired incorrectly).
- Affects livepanel tiles that rely on real-time aggregated metrics (per-tenant rollups) and those that use sliding-window aggregation with low-cardinality keys.

Root cause (findings):
- Metric-fanout path introduced intermittent backpressure when the ingest-router rebalanced during region failover. Backpressure caused a small subset of per-tenant fanout workers to drop an async ack/flush signal for the active aggregation window (race between flushTimer and rehydrate on failover).
- Missing flush/ack resulted in two observable failures: 1) the aggregator marked the window as complete with an empty bucket (treated as zero), and 2) the livepanel cache layer recorded a tombstone for that tile's timeseries segment. Both behaviors produced the displayed zero values.
- Root cause code area: ingest-router -> fanout worker pool -> aggregator window flush logic (files: ingest/router.go, fanout/worker_pool.py, aggregator/window_manager.rs).

Reproduction steps:
1) Start a small-scale staging cluster with simulated multi-region routing (route A and route B).
2) Produce a sustained burst of low-cardinality metrics (1-2 tokens per tenant) at ~200 TPS for 90s.
3) Trigger a route rebalance (simulate region failover).
4) Observe missed ack/flush logs and livepanel tile showing 0 for the affected window in the console.

Proposed fix (implementation plan):
- Short-term hotfix (canary before full rollout): add idempotent window flush with explicit flush tokens and ack retries. When a fanout worker is about to rehydrate or exit due to rebalance, it must publish a 'pre-flush' token and wait up to 250ms for ACK before proceeding. This prevents tombstone creation on transient rebalances.
- Medium-term: introduce explicit per-window watermark propagation across fanout workers (vector: window_id + sequence) so any worker that sees a late write can reconcile instead of writing a zero/tombstone.
- Long-term: augment the livepanel cache layer to treat an unexpected empty window as 'unknown' rather than zero, and surface a transient badge to users. Also add a reconciliation backfill job that looks for tombstone windows and rehydrates from the committed ingest log.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests around window flush idempotency and ack retry.
- Integration tests in staging with the failover simulation harness (added test scenario: rebalance_with_burst).
- Canary rollout to 5% of traffic on Hosted and one Dedicated tenant with replication; monitor new metrics (fanout_flush_ack_latency, fanout_late_writes, livepanel_tombstone_rate).
- Gradual 25/50/100 rollout with 30m monitoring windows and kill-switch in console for immediate rollback.

Monitoring/alerting changes to add:
- Alert: fanout_late_writes > 5/min per region -> P1
- Dashboards: livepanel_tombstone_rate by tenant, fanout_ack_retry_rate, window_reconcile_rate
- Add synthetic check: every 5m validate that livepanel tiles for a probe tenant show non-zero values when upstream telemetry exists.

Artifacts and links:
- Runbook (initial triage + mitigation): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Livepanel+Zero+Widgets+Runbook
- Failover simulation harness (internal repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-test-harness/pull/112
- Draft PR for hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8745 (branch: fix/fanout-preflush-acks)
- Staging dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/livepanel-incident

Security & compliance notes:
- Fix does not alter customer telemetry payloads or retention. No PII exposure. No KMS change required. Security review not required for the short-term patch (confirmed by security).

SLA/Customer communication:
- PM and Support to prepare targeted emails to affected customers with timelines and mitigation steps. We will offer a postmortem and indicate the timeline for the reconciliation backfill job if applicable.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage logged after PagerDuty escalations; assigned to Marco Nguyen for root cause analysis.

2026-03-11 - Marco Nguyen: Reproduced locally with failover harness; confirmed missing ack path in fanout worker during shutdown; captured logs and stack traces. Uploaded core logs to S3: s3://rwd-obs-logs/ENG-743500/replicate1.log

2026-03-12 - Marco Nguyen: Opened draft hotfix PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8745). Added unit tests for pre-flush ack retry. Requesting review from Ingrid Park (aggregator owner) and Ravi Desai (ingest-router).

2026-03-12 - Ingrid Park: Reviewed PR; suggested increasing ack wait to 300ms and adding metric for ack retry count. Also noted a race in window_manager.rs when window_id wraps — added suggestion to add a monotonic sequence tag.
2026-03-13 - Marco Nguyen: Incorporated Ingrid feedback; pushed updated PR. Kicked off staging Canary run. Initial canary metrics show fanout_tombstone_rate reduced by 92% in the test tenant.
2026-03-13 - Support (Lina Ortiz): Notified 3 impacted customers with mitigation steps and temporary alert suppression guidance. Customers responded that tile behavior improved during canary window.
